video_title: NBA VP Monty McCutchen says WHAT about the potential missed foul w/ Wemby & Brunson?! | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown criticizes free throw discrepancy in NBA Finals Game 3
quotes.excerpt: I never thought I'd see that in an NBA Finals game.
quotes.quote: To go 24 free throw attempts in a second half, that's 48 for the game if you think about it the way that they called that second half, compared to eight. All the shots we took, we got fouled four times roughly for eight free throw attempts. Again, I don't complain much. I never thought I'd see that in an NBA Finals game.

quotes.speaker: Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns takes accountability for Knicks loss in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: I didn't execute, didn't do what got us 13 straight wins in a row. That's how you lose.
quotes.quote: I didn't execute, didn't do what got us 13 straight wins in a row. That's how you lose a game. We didn't do what we've been doing for 13.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen explains the difference between equitable and fair officiating
quotes.excerpt: Fair and equitable are not the same thing. Equitable would mean the exact same amount of free throws.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: You said that equity and it's not the same, equity is not the same as fairness.

text_blocks.speaker: Monty McCutchen
text_blocks.text: Fair and equitable are not the same thing. Equitable would mean the exact same amount of free throws, which is being referenced here. But fair is calling similar plays similarly. And we've got to make sure that for our consistency as referees, that if the same types of plays are taking place, that they're called the same.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen admits a foul was missed on Victor Wembanyama play

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: There was an incident where Victor Wembanyama shoved Jalen Brunson in the back and no foul was called.

text_blocks.speaker: Monty McCutchen
text_blocks.text: We can all agree that a foul was missed on that play. We have a big part of our job is on-ball, off-ball exchanges between referees. We did a poor job of that here where we got two people on-ball and we don't see the screening action.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen discusses the importance of language in officiating
quotes.excerpt: Hit and push are two different things in that way, and I think that leads to a demarcation line.
quotes.quote: Language is really important here. Hit and push are two different things in that way, and I think that leads to a demarcation line. Most certainly the passion we're seeing in this series is what our fans and what the whole world is responding to.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen on the difficulty of officiating high-intensity playoff games
quotes.excerpt: The best sport represents that intensity. It lives on the edge of what is legal and not legal.
quotes.quote: The best sport represents that intensity. It lives on the edge of what is legal and not legal. That makes refereeing it very much more difficult than let's say in the middle of November, because every player is playing to the full limit and pushing all the envelopes they can to get that small margin of victory out.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen on the need for referees to let action dictate decisions
quotes.excerpt: Any good referee, when they're coming into the best time of the year, is aware of what is possible.
quotes.quote: Any good referee, when they're coming into the best time of the year, is aware of what is possible, but they have to let the action actually dictate their decisions. To be unaware would put you on your heels. To anticipate past what actually happens then means that you're making decisions that aren't warranted and would stifle the game.

quotes.speaker: Monty McCutchen
quotes.summary_phrase: Monty McCutchen addresses the confusion during the Jalen Brunson inbound play

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: Jaylen Brunson throws the ball off of Devin Vassell and the ruling is out of bounds, Knicks ball. But then Mitch Johnson signals to Dylan Harper to sub in to give them additional time to potentially challenge, but Dylan Harper just ran onto the court and the ball was inbounded. So what should have been the ruling?

text_blocks.speaker: Monty McCutchen
text_blocks.text: There's a really important part of refereeing that is running the game. You have to run the game with a certain authority that isn't overly authoritative, which can be off-putting, but also not to be in a situation in which you allow confusion to breathe, which is exactly what happened. I would have loved for it to have been a little more authoritative and really run that situation. I think we contributed to the confusion by not being more authoritative in that regard.
